context: Kenji takes Sho-young to an old-school arcade; observation.
purpose: Mentor and child sharing nostalgic outing.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 翔、この間来た時、楽しかったやろ?
lines.en: You know, you had fun the last time you came by, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, reflective opening. Soft Kansai inflection. Speaking to a child he's genuinely fond of — gentle encouragement mixed with real fondness. Pace is easy, unhurried.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 夢中になっちゃう、楽しい!
lines.en: I get really into it — it's so fun!
lines.style: Bright, unselfconscious enthusiasm. Quick, light delivery. The natural energy of a six-year-old who's discovered something that captures his whole attention. No self-consciousness, just genuine absorption.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 気楽に、ようけ遊んでいきや。
lines.en: Come on then, play as much as you want without worrying about it.
lines.style: Encouraging and permissive. Warm Kansai rhythm. Leaning in slightly — the tone of someone giving a child permission to be fully himself. Patient, gentle, genuinely wanting him to enjoy it.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 熱心、皆さん、ようけやってますね!
lines.en: Everyone here is working on it so seriously!
lines.style: Quiet observation with genuine wonder. Soft, thoughtful pace. The perceptiveness of a child noticing something adults might miss — impressed but not jealous, just noticing the dedication around him.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 盛り上がり、ええ場所やな。
lines.en: This is such a good place to be, isn't it?
lines.style: Content and settled. Warm, reflective Kansai cadence. Speaking as much to himself as to Sho — a moment of quiet satisfaction. Slow, appreciative pace.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Can I invite some of my classmates?
lines.style: Eager but not demanding. Slight upward lift on the question. A child checking boundaries, genuinely wanting to share something he's found. Hopeful, sincere, not manipulative.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: おう、尽くしてくれる、ええ友達連れて来や!
lines.en: Yeah, bring your good friends over — the ones who stick by you.
lines.style: Warm Kansai mentor voice. Slight emphasis on 'good friends' — not just anyone, but the ones worth bringing. Generous and encouraging. The tone of someone who sees character in the boy and wants to help him share what he loves.
